result.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. We introduce the Multimodal Concept Lens (MC-Lens), a multimodal Jacobian lens, to study these functions in VLM concept processing. Its vision encoder and language decoder lenses map intermediate states to a shared semantic space defined by the decoder's output vocabulary to compare concept accessibility across modalities. MC-Lens supports internal concept interventions to examine the role of accessed concepts in downstream computation. (i) Accessibility and selective access. Multimodal concept information is readable in intermediate states and selectively accessible as tasks require. We extend "readout carriers" from one name token to a token set to better capture and express concept information and support counterfactual experiments. (ii) Concepts in downstream computation. Counterfactual experiments show that accessed concept information participates in downstream computation and reasoning. (iii) Development of cross-modal alignment and selective access. We develop two J-space metrics tracking the development of cross-modal concept alignment more clearly than hidden state cosine in controlled VLM training. The experiment also shows that reliable selective access develops later than concept accessibility. (iv) Shared functions across models. Across VLM families and sizes, we find shared patterns of concept accessibility, query-dependent selectivity and cross-task intervention effects despite differences in internal organisation. These findings offer an experimental basis to study GWT in multimodal artificial systems and how it can guide cross-modal alignment improvements.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Multimodal Concept Lens（MC-Lens），一种多模态 Jacobian lens，将视觉编码器与语言解码器的中间状态映射到解码器词表定义的共享语义空间，比较跨模态概念的可读性与按需选择性访问，并用反事实干预检验被访问概念是否参与下游计算；另提出两个 J-space 指标追踪跨模态概念对齐的发展。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 LVR 关心的「视觉信息是否保留在内部状态」与「答案是否真正使用 latent 内容」：其概念可读性探针和干预方法可供核查视觉旁路、信息坍缩与贡献分配，J-space 指标也可能用于观察跨模态对齐与表示几何。
